slides.title: Routing Algorithms
content: Routing algorithms are mathematical methods used by routers to determine the best path for data packets based on distance, cost, and network conditions
Static routing uses manually configured routes that remain fixed and is suitable for small and stable networks
Dynamic routing automatically updates routing tables using protocols to adapt to network changes and failures
Common algorithms include Distance Vector (uses hop count), Link State (uses full network topology), and Hybrid routing methods

slides.title: Routing Protocols
content: Routing protocols are rules used by routers to exchange routing information and determine optimal paths for data transmission
Distance Vector protocols like RIP and EIGRP use metrics such as hop count and share routing tables with neighbors
Link State protocols like OSPF and IS-IS build a complete network map and calculate shortest paths using algorithms like Dijkstra
Protocols are categorized as Interior Gateway Protocols (IGP) for internal networks and Exterior Gateway Protocols (EGP) like BGP for internet routing

slides.title: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol)
content: BGP is a path vector routing protocol used for routing between autonomous systems on the internet
It uses attributes like AS_PATH to determine the best route and prevent routing loops
It operates over TCP and supports policy-based routing for flexible control of data flow
It is highly scalable and widely used in internet backbone routing and large enterprise networks

slides.title: Switching Techniques
content: Switching techniques define how data is transmitted across a network and how communication paths are established
Circuit switching establishes a dedicated path for continuous communication, used in telephone networks
Packet switching divides data into packets that travel independently and is used in modern internet communication
Message switching uses store-and-forward method where entire messages are sent and stored before forwarding

slides.title: Circuit vs Packet Switching
content: Circuit switching uses a dedicated path with guaranteed bandwidth and low delay but inefficient resource usage
Packet switching uses dynamic paths, efficient resource utilization, and supports large-scale networks like the internet
Packet switching may cause delays and out-of-order delivery, requiring reassembly at the destination
Circuit switching is suitable for real-time communication while packet switching is suitable for data communication

slides.title: Switching Importance
content: Switching enables efficient data transfer by managing communication paths and network traffic
It optimizes resource utilization by dynamically allocating bandwidth and avoiding congestion
It supports different communication types including real-time and non-real-time data transfer
Switching techniques are essential for scalable and reliable network architecture design
